documents.text: # # Procedure # # # # # # Indication # # # # * Suspicion of infection around implanted mechanical parts ( valves , pacemakers , electrodes , aortic stents ) * Investigation for bacterial emboli elsewhere in the body in case of bacteremia * Multiple forms of infection / inflammation + NB : Special preparation when investigating endocarditis * Certain neurodegenerative disorders 18 F-FDG PET is not suitable for diagnosing prostate cancer and pathology in the kidney / urinary tract pathology . # # # # Contraindications # # # # * None Diagnostic CT examination with i.v . contrast : Absolute : * Renal transplant recipients Relative : * Pregnancy * Dehydration * Significantly reduced eGFR ( eGFR < 45 mL / min ) * Diabetes mellitus , especially in case of significantly reduced eGFR and treatment with biguanides ( metformin ) such as Glucophage , Orabet or Avandamet * Dialysis * Multiple myeloma * Albuminuria * Elevated P-uric acid * Many contrast agent examinations within a short period of time * Thyrotoxicosis ( untreated ) * Amyloidosis * Myocardial infarction , acute or recent * Generally cardiac indisposed patients * Severe allergy , asthma * High fever * Treatment with nephrotoxica * Pheochromocytoma * Pregnancy # # # # Patient education : # # # # General : * Patients without diabetes should only drink tap water , medication should be taken as usual * In most cases , blood test results for P-Creatinine ( and eGFR ) must be available no later than the day before # # # # Diabetes : # # # # Insulin-dependent diabetes : * Patient should eat as usual and take regular insulin * The patient should * * not fast * At least 2 hours must pass from insulin administration until the scan can be performed ! During this period , the patient should only drink tap water Non-insulin-dependent diabetes : # # # # Examination principle # # # # PET : An injection of 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose ( 18 F-FDG ) is given while the patient is at rest . CT : Before the PET scan , a CT scan is performed , as this contains necessary information for optimal post-processing of the PET scan ( attenuation correction ) . The CT scan can be performed as either low-dose CT or as diagnostic CT - ideally with IV contrast if indicated . # # # # Execution # # # # A PVK is inserted into a vein in the elbow bend . The patient is injected with 1 ml corresponding to 1000 IU of unpreserved heparin . The patient then waits sitting / lying down for 1 hour , so that the 18 F-FDG is optimally distributed in the body . Before scanning The patient is sent to the toilet to urinate . The patient is positioned on on their back in the scanner - typically with their arms above their head . First , a CT scan is performed ( with or without contrast ) , which lasts about 5 minutes , followed by the first PET scan , which lasts about 25 minutes , and finally a PET scan over the heart which lasts approximately 8 minutes . The patient can leave the department when it has been verified that the examination has been completed satisfactorily . Patients with nephropathy : * If eGFR < 45 : The study is performed without IV contrast , in special cases and only after prior contact with the radiology department and specific prescription , the study can be performed with IV contrast . Duration : Approx . 2 hours in total , scan time approx . 35 minutes . # # # # Interpretation , answers and response times # # # # The scan is reviewed and it is assessed whether the distribution of 18 F-FDG is physiologic , abnormal or probably pathologic . For diagnostic CT , PET findings are conferred with the radiology department's CT findings before a final answer is given . * For PET with low-dose CT , an answer can usually be expected the following afternoon * For PET with diagnostic CT , a response can usually be expected two working days after the examination

documents.text: Symptoms are most often pain locally over the pseudoaneurysm . In worse cases threatened skin over the pseudoaneurysm or unstable hemodynamics with progressive size or active bleeding in additional tissue ( e.g . retroperitoneal ) . # # Procedure # # * * Investigation and referral to vascular clinic Pseudoaneurysms are most common in the inguinal arteries . For sizes up to to 2 cm , the natural history is usually benign as most thromboses occur spontaneously . For sizes of 2 - 3 cm , ultrasound-guided compression can be attempted over the accumulation for about 15 minutes , which can be repeated in case of partial thrombosis . This can be done at the local hospital , often with the assistance of radiology staff . In cases with inadequate treatment or complicated pathoanatomy , consider endovascular coiling or open surgery with exposure of the artery and sewing over the defect .

documents.text: The condition should be suspected in seizures with increased heart rate , respiration rate , BP and temperature , as well as sweating and dystonic movements / postures in a patient with severe acquired brain injury . The diagnosis is a clinical diagnosis and you can Baguley's scoring system PSH-AM ( see appendix 1 ) can be used as a basis . kidney stones , gallstones ) , hydrocephalus , epilepsy , withdrawal , etc . * Propanolol 20 - 80 mg every 6 hours per os : Good effect in tachycardia and hypertension as well as diaphoresis . * Opioid : Essential for pain . Fentanyl patches are preferable and , if possible , should be placed where sweating is less pronounced . * Gabapentin 100 - 300 mg every 8 hours . Can be quickly titrated up to a maximum of 4800 mg daily : No specific effect , but can improve most symptoms . * Baclofen 5 mg every 8 hours per os : Can be tried in dominant dystonic presentation . Intrathecal baclofen : In case of failure to control PSH on prophylactic tablet therapy , intrathecal baclofen may be considered and discussed at a conference . Decision can only be made by a specialist physician . It requires a neurosurgical procedure to apply the pump . * Clonazepam 0.5 - 2 mg every 8 hours per os . Effective for most symptoms . Must be tapered off slowly . * Bromocriptine 1.25 mg x 2 , increasing to max 40 mg / day . Can be tried if the above medications are not effective . The effect is not convincing and may come late . * Clonidine 0.1 to 0.3 mg every 6 to 8 hours per os . Can be given sc . This can be ordered at the department , but cannot be prescribed . A typical treatment may look as follows : Start with a dose of IV morphine ( starting dose 5 mg ) to interrupt a seizure of lasting more than a few minutes . Gabapentin can then be added with advantage ( starting dose 100 to 300 mg x 3 daily ) together with a non-selective Beta-blocker ( e.g . Propranolol starting dose of 10 mg x 3 daily ) . Frequent medication medication adjustment is needed for the first few days before the situation settles down . # # # # # # Monitoring # # # # # # The effect of the treatment should be monitored by daily review of seizure registration in Health Platform on a daily basis . The duration of PSH can vary from a few weeks to months , which is why any tapering of treatment must be assessed on an ongoing basis according to clinical assessment .

documents.text: # # Procedure # # * * General : * * B uses low molecular weight heparin ( Innohep ) for heparinization during hemodialysis treatment . As a general rule , the single-use syringes are used for all patients receiving more than 2500 IU , as they are cheaper and preservative-free . For patients receiving less than 2500 IU or more than 4500 IU innohep , draw up with 1 ml syringe from vial containing 10,000 IU / ml . * REMEMBER the date on the vial when breaking it . * The vial must not be stored above 25 ºC and * Must be used within 14 days . The medication is administered in the vein-side nozzle . * * New patient heparinization : * * Many patients can run an HD without the need for heparinization . The doctor has assessed this when prescribing the dialysis . Unless there are contraindications , 2500 IU Innohep is given as a bolus at start of hemodialysis . For dialysis treatment for more than 4 hours , an additional an additional 500 - 1000 IU Innohep is given from the start . * * Adjustment of the Innohep dose : * * * In case of clogging of the filter and / or abundant thrombi in the venous chamber , increase the starting bolus of Innohep by 500 - 1000 IU at the next HD . + NOTE : There must have been streaks + clots on more than 2 dialyses that are not due to blood pump stoppage x many during HD ( possibly due to dysfunctional vessel access ) . * If fistula compression time is repeatedly more than 30 minutes , the dose is reduced by 500 IU per hemodialysis until streaks / clots are observed in the filter , artery and / or vein chamber . The dose is then increased with 500 IU Innohep . + Note : If the compression time is long despite a striated filter and thrombi in the venous chamber , it may be a sign of stenosis in the fistula * The hemodialysis nurse can change the dose according to the above instructions , but Innohep must be prescribed by a doctor the first time it is given . * If there is a white filter and no thrombi in the venous chamber , the dose is reduced by 500 IU at the next HD , and so on .

documents.text: There are many reasons why a child may need a tracheostomy tube , such as for example : * Long-term ventilator treatment * Congenital malformations * Sequelae after long-term ventilator treatment * Stenoses / malasias in the larynx / trachea * Congenital recurrent paresis * Viruses , edema , tumors , surgical procedures * Swallowing problems / false swallowing * Neck and facial trauma * Reduced coughing power and great difficulty mobilizing secretions * Neuromuscular disorders with reduced muscle strength , including in the respiratory muscles The tube is placed between the first and second tracheal ring in the trachea while the child is under general anesthesia . The length of time the child needs the tube varies varies greatly . If the tracheostomy is expected to be needed for a longer period of time ( months , years or permanently ) and as soon as the child's condition is stable , contact RCØ ( Rspiration Center East at Glostrup Hospital ) , with a view to going home with a tracheostomy . Once the parents have completed the the training program , they are free to leave the ward with their child . However , they must spend the night in 5061 for monitoring purposes . In some cases , this can be deviate from this .

documents.text: # # Procedure # # # # Subcutaneous abscesses can basically be treated in the following two ways : 1 . conventional treatment 2 . primary suturing under antibiotic coverage * * Conventional treatment The skin flap is removed from the abscess , the septae are broken down and the abscess contents are drained . A hemostatic mech is placed in the cavity . Change after approx . 24 hours + / - . anesthesia by individual assessment . * * Primary suturing under antibiotic coverage Incision over the apex of the abscess , the abscess contents are drained and the septae digitally decompose the septae . Then curettage with a sharp spoon . The cavity is irrigated , close with penetrating prolene ( 1 - 0 or 2 - 0 ) on a large needle . The suture is placed as shown in the figure below . Give antibiotics according to instructions . instructions . Do * not * culture from abscesses , except for suspected air-generating infections ( see instructions for necrotizing soft tissue infections ) . * * Guidelines for the treatment of abscesses Most abscesses can be treated with primary sutures under antibiotic coverage . 1 .
